solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Upper limit on wages that provides closure (5,3)

definitions.note: a relative-clause definition: the thing that provides closure

indicators.note: an upper limit placed 'on' wages sits after them in an across answer, so CAP follows SCREW

blocks.note: screw is old British slang for wages
a cap is an upper limit

annotation.surface: A pay cap imposed on workers, presented as a satisfying resolution.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upper limit on wages' reads as a pay cap, one phrase; split it and 'wages' is SCREW, slang for pay. 'Closure' teases the emotional sense but means sealing a bottle.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic-leaning description: a screw cap is the twist-on lid that closes a bottle or jar.

entries.clue: Save sailor on vacation (4,4)

blocks.note: an old salt is a sailor

annotation.surface: Someone rescuing a sailor who is off on holiday.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Save' looks like a rescue; it is the money sense, putting something by.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from preserving food in salt: to salt money away is to hoard it, the thrifty sense of save.

entries.clue: Airline backs peculiar measure (5)

indicators.note: to back is to support from behind, so BA stands after RUM

annotation.surface: An airline supporting some odd policy measure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backs' is not a turnaround here: BA backs RUM by standing behind it.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary sense: a measure is an old word for a dance, and the rumba is one particular dance.

entries.clue: External cladding moulded to be hard wearing (15)

indicators.note: what is moulded is pressed into a new shape, so the letters take a new form

annotation.surface: A spec for house cladding that is moulded to be durable.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To be' looks like a link but its letters are fodder: all fifteen letters of 'to be hard wearing' are needed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: weatherboarding is overlapping boards fixed to a building's outside walls against the weather.

entries.clue: Angry alpha male finally rebuked (7)

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the end letter of 'male' is used

blocks.note: A = alpha in the NATO alphabet
to rate is an old word for to scold

annotation.surface: A dominant man who gets cross after being told off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Alpha male' reads as one phrase; split, alpha is A and 'male finally' is E.
annotation.definitionFit: A British colloquialism: someone aerated is worked up, fizzing like a carbonated drink, so angry.

entries.clue: Lizard Island drifting west in South American region (6)

indicators.note: west is leftwards on a map and in an across answer, so the I inside drifts to the front

blocks.note: GUIANA with its I taken out to move

annotation.surface: A lizard on an island that floats westward off South America.
annotation.walkthrough: The region is GUIANA; the island is its own I, which shifts left to the front.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain category: the iguana is a large tropical American lizard.

entries.clue: Shake water right off big fish (5,5,5)

indicators.note: food that is off has gone bad, spoilt, so the letters are spoilt out of order

annotation.surface: A big fish thrashing to shake the water off itself.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shake' begs to be the anagram indicator, and 'right off' to drop an R; both are fodder, and 'off' alone does the scrambling.
annotation.definitionFit: A deliberately understated description: the great white is the largest predatory fish, a very big fish indeed.

entries.clue: New order of “pain”, “toast” or “bruschetta”? (9)

indicators.note: a new order of the letters is a rearrangement of them

annotation.surface: A diner ordering bread under its French, English and Italian names.
annotation.walkthrough: Pain is French for bread, so the list looks like translations; only its letters matter. The question mark flags a definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: bruschetta, toasted bread with toppings, is a typical Italian antipasto or starter.

entries.clue: Jeer after bishop leaves drink (6)

indicators.note: what remains of the jeer once the bishop has walked out of it, so B is dropped

blocks.note: B = bishop in chess notation, removed

annotation.surface: Heckling after a bishop walks out, then a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: To barrack, jeering at a speaker, is chiefly British and Australian.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain category: arrack is a strong Asian spirit distilled from palm sap or rice, so a drink.

entries.clue: American government agency controlling most of car plant (6)

indicators.note: to control something is to hold it, so A CIA holds CA within
most but not all of the word, so its last letter goes

annotation.surface: A US agency seizing control of most of a car factory.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Car plant' reads as a factory, one phrase; 'plant' is the definition on its own. 'American government agency' is two pieces, which is what lets the container fit between them.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain category: the acacia, often called wattle, is a tree or shrub, so a plant.

entries.clue: Beginning to learn novel mathematical premise (5)

indicators.note: the beginning of 'learn' is its first letter

annotation.surface: A student starting to learn about a new idea in mathematics.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like 'new'; it is a specific novel.
annotation.definitionFit: A technical sense: a lemma is a subsidiary proposition proved and then used as a premise towards a larger theorem.

entries.clue: Her escort worked in Kentish Town (9)

indicators.note: material that is worked is kneaded into a new shape, so the letters are reshaped

annotation.surface: A woman's escort had a job in Kentish Town, a district of north London.
annotation.walkthrough: Kentish Town is a real part of London, which steers you away; read it as a town in Kent, the county south-east of London.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example with a pun: Rochester, a cathedral city on the Medway, is one town in Kent.

entries.clue: American newsreel producer notes lacking passion (9)

blocks.note: two notes: TI from the sol-fa scale and C

annotation.surface: An American newsreel producer's notes show no enthusiasm.
annotation.walkthrough: Pathé's newsreels ran in British cinemas for most of the 20th century.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from the Greek for without feeling: the apathetic have no passion.

entries.clue: “Matter closed” — Head of Police in command (5)

indicators.note: the head of a word is its top, its first letter

blocks.note: a door pushed to is closed

annotation.surface: A police chief declaring a case closed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Matter closed' reads as a case being shut; 'Matter' is the definition and 'closed' gives TO, as in pushing a door to.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the matter under discussion is the topic.

entries.clue: Highly regarded opening pair in Adelaide bogged down (7)

indicators.note: in cricket the opening pair go in first, so the first two letters

annotation.surface: A respected pair of opening batsmen getting stuck at the cricket in Adelaide.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Opening pair' is cricket talk for the two batsmen who start an innings; here it means the first two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to be admired is to be held in high regard.

entries.clue: Funny chap’s mum upset king outside factory (3,6)

indicators.note: in a down answer, to upset something is to tip it over, so REX reads upwards
the reversed king stands outside the factory, round MILL

blocks.note: Latin rex = king, reversed to XER

annotation.surface: A comedian whose mother annoyed a king standing outside a factory.
annotation.walkthrough: Max Miller was a famously risqué British music-hall comedian. The reversed king is split in two, which hides the Latin word well.
annotation.definitionFit: A description of a person: Max Miller, 'the Cheeky Chappie', made a living being a funny chap.

entries.clue: Horrified — Reichstag has tartan curtains! (6)

indicators.note: curtains screen what is behind them, so the answer is screened inside the words

annotation.surface: Outrage that the German parliament has hung tartan curtains.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Has' looks like the link that says 'contains', but its letters are part of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to be aghast is to be struck with horror.

entries.clue: Fashionable apartment Enid vacated and blew up (8)

indicators.note: a vacated place has been emptied, so ENID loses its inside letters

annotation.surface: Enid moved out of her trendy flat and then lost her temper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vacated' fits the flat so well that it seems to be about moving out; it empties Enid instead.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past tense: to blow up a balloon is to inflate it.

entries.clue: Long stretches keeping 90 people out of prison (2-4)

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so EONS holds XC inside

blocks.note: eons are long stretches of time

annotation.surface: Long prison sentences keeping ninety people locked up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stretches' sounds like prison sentences, fitting the surface; here they are just long periods.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang term: an ex-con is a former convict, someone released from prison.

entries.clue: Very wide titfer. And? (2,4)

blocks.note: titfer = hat, from Cockney rhyming slang tit-for-tat

annotation.surface: A remark about an enormous hat, met with a shrug of 'And?'.
annotation.walkthrough: Titfer is Cockney rhyming slang: tit-for-tat rhymes with hat.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a flat 'And?' is a dismissive retort meaning 'so what?'.

entries.clue: Digital cash tech firm trashed? (7)

indicators.note: something trashed is binned, put in the bin, so IT CO goes inside BIN

annotation.surface: A cryptocurrency company that has failed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trashed' does two jobs: it names the BIN and says to put something in it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Bitcoin is the best-known cryptocurrency, money that exists only digitally.

entries.clue: British daredevil more vigorous (7)

annotation.surface: A British stuntman who is more energetic than the rest.
annotation.walkthrough: British is usually BR, which leaves one R too many; here it is just B.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the comparative: brisk means lively and energetic.

entries.clue: Hoodlum regularly lost East Side’s premier detective (6)

indicators.note: letters lost at regular intervals, so every other letter goes
premier means first, so the first letter of 'Side'

blocks.note: H, O, L, M: the 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th letters of 'hoodlum'

annotation.surface: A gangster lost on New York's East Side, and the city's best detective.
annotation.walkthrough: 'East Side' reads as a place in New York; split, it gives E and then the first letter of Side.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Sherlock Holmes is the archetypal fictional detective.

entries.clue: Tree, very large, that is by river (5)

annotation.surface: A very large tree standing by a river.
annotation.walkthrough: OS for outsize is a British clothing label.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the osier is a willow grown for basket-making, a tree of riverbanks.

entries.clue: Fantastic hour visiting West End theatre production’s not suitable for all (9)

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone's place, so H goes inside W1
the musical is 'not suitable for all', so it has no U

blocks.note: W1 is the London postcode of the West End; the 1 reads as I
a musical is a theatre production
U = universal, the British film certificate for all ages; removed

annotation.surface: A fantastic West End musical rated too racy for children.
annotation.walkthrough: W1 is the West End's London postcode, and the digit 1 stands in for I. U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym in the fanciful sense: fantastic here means driven by fancy, not excellent.

entries.clue: Affordable energy fills crack (5)

blocks.note: to chap is to crack, as skin does in the cold

annotation.surface: Cheap power fills a gap in the market.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crack' suggests a fissure; it is chapped skin.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what is cheap costs little, so is affordable.

entries.clue: When jogging, a kilt must perform various functions (9)

indicators.note: jogging jolts and jostles, knocking the letters out of place

entries.clue: Expert Head of Art Department (5)

indicators.note: the head of a word is its top, its first letter

annotation.walkthrough: The capitals make it look like a job title, 'Head of Art Department'.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun synonym from the alchemists' Latin adeptus, one who has attained the secret: an adept is a skilled expert.

entries.clue: Quiet game golf — son expresses indifference (6)

blocks.note: G = golf in the NATO alphabet

annotation.walkthrough: 'Game golf' reads as one phrase; the game is rugby union and golf is just G.

entries.clue: Roué moved into bachelor flat as part of slowing-down process (5,3)
